red_then_green.what_it_was: a production defect: `without_the_endpoint` did not exist, so a transport error's own text — which quotes the URL it was posting to — was written verbatim into the submission answer, credential and all

my own over-claim, not a defect: the assertion demanded `eth_sendRawTransaction` inside the *read* half's phrase, i.e. it asserted a composition the design does not use. The send phrase names the socket only; the method belongs to the answer text around it
red_then_green.resolution: the method checks moved onto the composed lines (the shared helper asserts `contains(eth_sendRawTransaction)` and `!contains(eth_getTransactionReceipt)` there), and line 514 now asserts the phrase/socket split

url_leak_measurement.method: grep -o 'http://127\.0\.0\.1:[0-9]*' over each run's own log — a count, deliberately not the URL itself, which carried a credential-shaped path segment
url_leak_measurement.post_fix_note: the green run printed no panic message at all, so it printed no line to leak; the standing guarantee is the assertion, not the log: endpoint_provenance.rs:278 and :503 fail if any composed line or evidence row contains the planted credential
url_leak_measurement.stub_url_shape: http://127.0.0.1:{ephemeral port}/token/abc123 — an authority and a path token are both things a submission line must not repeat, and loopback is §5's first bullet made executable: a localhost socket is not automatically labelled local

label_vocabulary.read_side: evm_chain::EndpointPurpose — LocalCanonicalRpc | PublicCanonicalRpc | LocalFlashblocksRpc | PublicFlashblocksRpc | Unknown (default), operator-declared, unchanged by this milestone
label_vocabulary.submit_side_before: EndpointKind::PublicHttpRpc, hard-coded at both lane construction sites; its wire word was `public_http_rpc`
label_vocabulary.submit_side_after: EndpointKind::Unknown, hard-coded at both lane construction sites; its wire word is `unknown`
kept_on_purpose: PublicHttpRpc and FlashblocksHttpRpc stay in the enum for a caller that was *told* who runs its endpoint; `the_read_sides_label_never_crosses_into_the_submission_path` asserts the words are still constructible in `submitter.rs`, so the zeros it reports are a retirement at the wiring and not a rename out of reach of the scan

EndpointKind::Unknown.may_broadcast() is true: the question that predicate answers is whether the socket can carry a send, and refusing to send over an unknown endpoint would be the opposite guess — that not knowing is a safety property
EndpointKind::Recorded.may_broadcast() stays false and `execution_that_does_not_fit_the_configuration_is_refused_before_the_socket` proves the refusal happens before a byte leaves

production_sites.measured_by: endpoint_provenance.rs asserts exactly 2 occurrences of `EndpointKind::Unknown` across those two files, and 0 of `EndpointKind::PublicHttpRpc`; a third site would mean a new path choosing its own class
production_sites.remaining_public_http_rpc_literal_sites_: 13, every one below its file's `#[cfg(test)]` marker (submitter.rs, evidence.rs, lifecycle.rs) — classified by position, not by filename
production_sites.rpc_methods: no new JSON-RPC method; `eth_sendRawTransaction`'s call shape is untouched

redaction_rule.submission_provenance: over endpoint rpc-<16 hex of keccak256(url)> — names the socket, claims no class
redaction_rule.without_the_endpoint: replaces both reqwest shapes (the URL as configured, and the URL with a trailing slash the client normalized in) with the same digest; applied to the two error arms of `submit()` — the JSON-RPC refusal and the transport/no-answer path
redaction_rule.why_the_digest_and_not_a_drop: §25 forbids paraphrasing what the node's transport said, so the message travels unchanged and only the endpoint is taken back out
redaction_rule.composition: all four answer strings interpolate `({provenance})`; the accepted branch keeps the node's returned value, the unknown branch keeps what the body said, and the read/submit vocabularies stay separate — a submission line never contains `eth_getTransactionReceipt`

historical_rows_left_alone.rule: §9 forbids reprinting or rewriting M10 and other historical evidence, so the class word is retired forward-only
historical_rows_left_alone.measurement: counted over `git ls-files data/evidence` (1382 tracked files) by a read-only scan, not by the gate

holes_left_open.hole: a gateway that answers with only the URL *path* (where a key or JWT lives) rather than the whole URL leaves the scrub untouched — `without_the_endpoint` replaces the configured URL and that URL plus a slash, not a fragment of it
holes_left_open.why_not_fixed_here: closing it means redacting the message, which §25 forbids; the same asymmetry was recorded on the trace side in M12-B and left the same way
holes_left_open.suggested_milestone: an outbound redaction contract for error bodies, if a real endpoint is ever reached with credentials in its path

holes_left_open.hole: the read path's error strings are not scrubbed: `read_error` in sequencer_direct.rs builds `ExecutionError` display text from the transport's own message, which can quote the URL
holes_left_open.why_not_fixed_here: every call site of `read_error` that this milestone can reach terminates in a log line, not an evidence row, and sweeping it would widen the production diff past the defect class (§9's scope discipline)
holes_left_open.suggested_milestone: the same rule applied to read-side strings before any read error is written into evidence

holes_left_open.hole: the accepted branch interpolates the node's raw result value unscrubbed
holes_left_open.why_not_fixed_here: the value is the JSON-RPC `result` for a send (a hash) or the body of a non-hash answer; the URL would have to be echoed back by the node into its own result, which is the gateway case above

observations_for_the_report: the transport retries a *send*: crates/chain/src/rpc.rs:212 loops at most twice for any method, so a dropped answer to `eth_sendRawTransaction` can mean two posts of the same payload — the lane's one-send assertion is about the lane, not the wire (out of scope here, §9)
